AUDIO IMPORTANT:

if there is no audio in your video-in then it errors. 

If you have silent video, you will need to provide audio in of some kind to run the workflow, even if you dont include it in the output video. Use the audio loader to load in a random mp3 (e.g. 10 seconds of music or ambient silence) and set duration to match your inbound video. swithc the audio vae encoder to use this not the video. This should then work.

NOTE: I found if I prompt for "non_diegetic_music:" it will then use it rather than the audio, so make sure to put "N/A" in any audio descriptors for the prompt if you want to keep the audio you are loading in.

shows scale size to achieve MP provided. less than 1.0 means the inbound video was larger than the mp value. (do a test run first then cancel it to get that info)

I target 2mp usually but some might be able to go higher. (15 sec video at 2mp is going to take 30 mins so be warned).

(I could get 3mp for 8 second video in 30 mins, using pika lora, set 2 step manual sigmas to 0.7, 0.49, 0 with euler sampler, attempts to try the clownscheduler oomed at 3mp.)

context windows nodes from https://github.com/ckinpdx/ComfyUI-MMH3Tools you can get to 2mp as it context windows the run splitting it up and uses less VRAM that way.

# MarkDKBerry.com

YouTube: [https://www.youtube.com/@markdkberry](https://www.youtube.com/@markdkberry)

Patreon: [https://www.patreon.com/c/AIMakingMovies](https://www.patreon.com/c/AIMakingMovies)

Workflows: [https://github.com/mdkberry/comfyui_workflows](https://github.com/mdkberry/comfyui_workflows)

---

**You will need to install [https://github.com/ckinpdx/ComfyUI-MMH3Tools](https://github.com/ckinpdx/ComfyUI-MMH3Tools) for this workflow.** If you have a Low or MidVRAM (12GB VRAM) card this workflow should work for you, if you have a bigger card, you might want to test ckinpdx upscale workflows instead. 

It works by "context window" splitting the total frames (e.g. 192 frame video split to two segments, so you can get to the magical 2mp for 8 second clips as I did in tests, even on a 3060 RTX. You max VRAM is then used on each split segment thus giving you better reach. Amazingly it was still faster than my other upscaler workflows.

---

**Updated**: 25th August 2026. *(replaced batch image list node with MMH3 Image List node. changed sampler and sigma settings .)*

**Useage**: *Single pass v2v pixel space upscaler with context windows to split use of the VRAM across multiple segments, making higher resolution possible for longer clips on lowerVRAM.*


---

## USING THIS WORKFLOW

***UPDATE NOTE: I could get 3mp for 8 second video in 30 mins, using pika lora, set 2 step manual sigmas to 0.7, 0.49, 0 with euler sampler, attempts to try the clownscheduler oomed at 3mp and occasional runs failed but its the best I have achieved so far - Mark, 2n Nov 2026.)***


**Get a structural video made elsewhere, then import it here for detailing.** (its best if you use fairly high quality result coming in, I found 1824 x 736 was good that needed eyes fixing a bit and blemishes. For stronger fixing, you might need to increase denoise or steps. I havent tested it for that yet.)

**Set to chosen megapixel upscale size I can do 2mp for 8 seconds in this workflow** (see the notes beside the video import node). Resize if you need to reduce the inbound video, upscale if you need to increase it. Size it to fit your VRAM and avoid ooms.

**I've been leaving the width and height of the actual "H3 Reference To Video Model" Node set to 1mp**. We know it to be the size the H3 model was trained on. But the important bit is the size of your inbound video and what you resize that to.

**The frame count of the video-in is used to define the length**, as such the duration has been disabled in this workflow. 

**Since this uses context windows, oom from longer videos is mitigated**. I have only tested 8 seconds long video so far and could get to 2mp with only 10.5GB VRAM being used. There is a spike going into  the sampler but it didnt oom on my setup with this workflow. Context windows is the reason for this. Its suprisingly fast, considering that, I was expecting it to take a lot longer.

**Make a new prompt and be sure to target the ref images correctly**. 

I am getting 8 second video done in 26 mins to 2mp. Longer clip length will probably work too due to the "context windows" from the ckinpdx custom node.

## ISSUES:

- You must provide audio to the workflow either from the inbound video, or by providing your own audio file. I have put a audio loader in there which you can reconnect (yellow vrs red reroute connector).

subject_definitions:
<Picture 1> is the first frame of [Shot 1], a wide 21:9 composition of a candlelit gothic drawing room with a stone fireplace on the left, a man seated in a carved armchair at centre-left, a blonde woman in a blue velvet gown seated beside him on the right, and a brunette woman in a red velvet gown leaning over the chair back between them.
<Subject 1> is the bald middle-aged man in <Picture 2>, shown full length and front facing in a black suit, white shirt and slim black tie, with a stern, weathered face. In <Picture 1> he sits in the armchair on the left.
<Subject 2> is the long-haired blonde woman in <Picture 3>, shown full length, front facing and barefoot in a blue velvet wrap gown with a deep V neckline. In <Picture 1> she sits on the right of the chair.
<Subject 3> is the dark-haired brunette woman in <Picture 4>, shown full length, front facing and barefoot in a burgundy-red velvet gown. In <Picture 1> she leans behind the chair with her arm along its back.
<Subject 4> is the decaying gothic mansion drawing room in <Picture 1>, with a large weathered stone fireplace with a lit log fire, a mantel crowded with white pillar candles, a standing candelabra on the right, peeling plaster walls in ochre and brown, heavy dark velvet drapes at the far right, and a thick, worn, deep-pile carpet covering the whole floor.
<Audio 1> is the voice-timbre reference for <Subject 3> (S1), a posh English female voice, slightly husky. <Subject 2> shares this voice but does not speak in this shot.
<Audio 2> is the voice-timbre reference for <Subject 1> (S2), a deep, gravelly American male voice.

summary:
[keyframe completion + reference generation + audio reference] A single continuous 15-second locked-off opening shot of a 1970s Hammer-style sapphic vampire gothic horror scene, beginning from <Picture 1>. <Subject 2> and <Subject 3> are vampires. <Subject 1> is their unaware guest and victim. <Subject 2> is nervous and silent while <Subject 3> goes to fetch wine. <Subject 3> returns carrying only a glass of red wine, hands it to <Subject 1> with her right hand and rests her left hand on the chair back. Only he drinks. All barefoot movement is completely silent. The voices follow <Audio 1> and <Audio 2> as timbre references only. There is no music.

retention_analysis:
<Picture 1> ([Shot 1] first frame): partially_preserved - the composition, set, lighting, costumes and seating positions are kept exactly. The one change is that the ambiguous hand at the centre of frame becomes <Subject 2>'s clearly attached right hand, brought into view by her own early movement.
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - face, bald head, black suit, white shirt, black tie and seated posture are retained.
<Subject 2> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - long straight blonde hair, blue velvet gown, bare feet and pale complexion are retained.
<Subject 3> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - dark wavy hair, burgundy velvet gown and bare feet are retained.
<Subject 4> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - fireplace, candles, candelabra, decayed walls and drapes are retained.
<Audio 1>: reference - the timbre and posh, slightly husky delivery guide <Subject 3>'s single line without copying the source signal.
<Audio 2>: reference - the deep, gravelly American timbre guides <Subject 1>'s single line without copying the source signal.

detailed_description:
The target video is a 1970s Hammer Horror gothic vampire scene, shot on Panasonic VariCam 35, ultra-smooth 180-degree shutter, shallow depth of field, anamorphic lens flare, Hammer Horror film aesthetic, Eastmancolor film stock, warm pushed saturation, slightly overexposed highlights, deep crushed shadows, lush theatrical lighting, gothic British period atmosphere, 1960s-1970s Bray Studios production design, velvet textures and rich decay, soft focus on backgrounds, cinematic 21:9 Ultrawide, smooth filmic motion, no digital sharpness, organic grain structure.
[Shot 1] The shot begins from <Picture 1>, a locked-off wide shot with no camera movement for the full 15 seconds. In <Subject 4>, the fireplace flames flicker on the left and candle flames sway gently on the mantel and the right-hand candelabra, throwing warm gold light across the peeling walls. <Subject 1>, the bald man in the black suit and loosened tie, sits stiffly in the carved armchair, one hand on the armrest. His eyes travel slowly around the room, up to the mantel candles, across the cracked plaster, then back to the fire, and he gives a small impressed breath and a slight nod as he weighs up the grand, decaying setting. <Subject 2>, the blonde in the blue velvet gown, sits close beside him, tense and silent. In the first two seconds she moves her right arm, drawing her right hand clearly out of her velvet sleeve and into the centre of the frame, and lets it settle on the chair arm near his before she nervously smooths the velvet over her knee. Her eyes dart to him, then away, and her lips press together in awkward unease. About three seconds in, <Subject 3>, the brunette in the burgundy gown, straightens from the chair back, gives <Subject 1> a lingering smile and glides barefoot out of frame to the left behind the chair across the deep-pile carpet, leaving the awkward pause. Her bare feet make no sound at all: there are no footsteps, no clicking, no clopping and no heel or shoe noise anywhere in the audio, only the faint whisper of her velvet gown. For several seconds <Subject 2> fidgets, steals another glance at <Subject 1>, shifts her bare foot on the carpet and swallows, while he keeps scanning the room without noticing her nerves. A faint trickle of wine being poured into a glass is heard from far off-screen. Around nine seconds in, <Subject 3> re-enters from the left, again completely silent on the carpet, carrying in her right hand a single glass of dark red wine. She holds no bottle and has nothing else in her hands. She stops beside the chair, extends the glass to <Subject 1> with her right hand and rests her left hand on the back of his chair.  Leaning in, <Subject 3> (S1) says in the posh, slightly husky English voice referenced from <Audio 1>, <d>[English] Here you are.</d> <Subject 1> (S2) takes the glass and replies in the deep gravelly American voice referenced from <Audio 2>, <d>[English] Thanks.</d> He sips. <Subject 3> and <Subject 2> do not drink. Both watch him, <Subject 3> with a faint knowing smile and <Subject 2> with her nervous gaze flicking to the glass at his lips. The shot holds on the three of them until the end.

overall_soundscape:
A hushed, cavernous room tone runs throughout, with soft crackling and popping from the log fire, faint candle flutter, gentle velvet and suit-fabric rustles, a creak of the carved chair, a faint wine pour from off-screen and the soft touch of the glass as it is handed over. No footstep sounds of any kind are present: no clip-clop, no heels, no shoes and no floor taps, because the women are barefoot on a thick, sound-deadening carpet and their movement is silent.

non_diegetic_music:
N/A
